trans.sense: to cause (rays of light, etc) to converge at a single point
(transitive, optics) to adjust (a lens, an optical instrument)
(intransitive) to concentrate one's attention on something

examples.text: The difficulties of focussing colour-light signals on curved tracks to ensure maximum sighting distance were underlined in the recent official report [...] on a low-speed collision at Newcastle Central on July 25, 1960, between an unfitted freight and a diesel-hauled passenger train.
examples.ref: 1961 February, “Talking of Trains: Collision at Newcastle”, in Trains Illustrated, pages 75–76:

raw_glosses: (transitive) To cause (rays of light, etc) to converge at a single point.
glosses: To cause (rays of light, etc) to converge at a single point.

examples.text: You'll need to focus the microscope carefully in order to capture the full detail of this surface.

raw_glosses: (transitive, optics) To adjust (a lens, an optical instrument) in order to position an image with respect to the focal plane.
glosses: To adjust (a lens, an optical instrument) in order to position an image with respect to the focal plane.

examples.text: I can't get the lens to focus.
The camera focuses automatically on the subject's eyes.

raw_glosses: (intransitive, optics, of a lens, optical instrument, etc.) To adjust itself or be adjusted such that light from a scene converges appropriately to create a clear image.
glosses: To adjust itself or be adjusted such that light from a scene converges appropriately to create a clear image.

examples.text: The president focused her remarks on the newcomers.

raw_glosses: (transitive) To direct attention, effort, or energy to a particular audience or task.
glosses: To direct attention, effort, or energy to a particular audience or task.

examples.text: If you're going to beat your competitors, you need to focus.
I have to focus on my work.

raw_glosses: (intransitive, followed by on or upon) To concentrate one's attention on something; to have as one's central point of interest, concern, etc.
glosses: To concentrate one's attention on something; to have as one's central point of interest, concern, etc.

examples.text: The text box won't receive the user's keystrokes unless you explicitly focus it.

raw_glosses: (computing, graphical user interface, transitive) To transfer the input focus to (a visual element), so that it receives subsequent input.
glosses: To transfer the input focus to (a visual element), so that it receives subsequent input.

examples.text: Whole pages of it are filled with masses of figures, generally single numbers added up in batches, and then the totals added in batches again, as though he were "focusing" some account, as the auditors put it.

raw_glosses: (accounting, formerly) To aggregate figures of accounts.

glosses: Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus (definite location).

examples.text: The disturbances at the periphery became a focal concern later in the investigation.

glosses: Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus of attention.

raw_glosses: (optics) A measure of how strongly an optical system converges or diverges light, the inverse of optical power. In the simple case of a single convex lens, it is the distance along the optical axis from the principal plane of the lens to the lens's focal point (where, for instance, the film would be placed in a camera). For more complex or multi-element optical systems, focal length need not correspond to any obvious measurable physical distance.
